projects.title: ConstructionPro — Professionals Nepal
projects.summary: A marketplace where families in Nepal find house designs with honest cost estimates and book the architects, engineers, interior designers and contractors who drew them.
projects.description: ConstructionPro connects people who want to build a house with the professionals who design them. Clients browse a design library with filters for budget, area and style, save favourites, book a consultation in a professional's free time slot, and chat in real time. Professionals manage their portfolio, availability and bookings from a dashboard, and admins moderate content and export reports.
features: Design library with search, filters, sorting and shareable URLs
Booking system built on each professional's published availability
Real-time messaging with online status and typing indicators (Socket.IO)
Role-based dashboards for clients, professionals and admins, with charts and CSV export
JWT authentication, image uploads, light and dark themes

projects.title: MCQPrep — Exam Practice App
projects.summary: MCQ practice for Nepal's entrance and competitive exams (IOE, IOM, KU, Loksewa) with instant feedback and an admin question bank.
projects.description: Students pick a course and subject and get questions they haven't seen yet, with the correct answer and an explanation shown as soon as they answer. Progress and accuracy are tracked per subject without needing an account. The redesign uses a warm paper-and-ink palette, OMR-style answer bubbles and a working sample question on the home page. Admins sign in to manage courses, subjects and the question bank.
features: No-repeat questions drawn from the ones a student hasn't answered yet
Answers are checked on the server, so the answer key never reaches the browser early
Try-one sample question on the home page that runs entirely in the browser
Progress bars, accuracy, session score, streaks and keyboard shortcuts (A–F, 1–6, Enter)
JWT-protected admin with dashboard, question bank search and a bulk-friendly editor

images.caption: Home page with a live sample question

projects.title: Larder — Grocery & Kitchen Store
projects.summary: An e-commerce storefront for groceries and kitchen goods: search, filters, a slide-out bag, promo codes, delivery slots and order history.
projects.description: Larder is a full shopping flow that runs entirely in the browser. Shoppers browse 62 real products across four aisles, search from anywhere with a keyboard shortcut, filter and sort with the state kept in the URL, fill a bag, apply a promo code, pick a delivery day and place an order. Cart, saved items and orders persist in localStorage, and every push is tested and deployed to GitHub Pages.
features: Instant search on / or Ctrl K with arrow-key navigation
Aisle, price, stock and rating filters with five sort orders, all shareable through the URL
Product pages with gallery, specs, reviews and related items
Slide-out bag, free-delivery progress, promo codes and a validated checkout with delivery slots
Order history and saved items, hand-drawn SVG icons and full keyboard accessibility

projects.title: Cardiac Risk — Heart Disease Prediction
projects.summary: A random forest that estimates heart disease risk from 13 clinical measurements, served through an interactive web app with live predictions and a full model report.
projects.description: A rebuild of my original notebook project. I found that the dataset's 1,125 rows were only 302 unique patients and that several codes (including the target) were inverted, fixed both, then compared four models with cross-validated grid search. The selected random forest is served by a FastAPI backend to a dependency-free web app where you can assess a patient live, try real held-out patients, or enter only the values you know and see an uncertainty range.
features: Data cleaning: removed duplicate patients and corrected mislabelled target, chest pain, slope and thal codes
Four models tuned with stratified 5-fold grid search; the winner is chosen on CV ROC-AUC, not the test set
Live risk estimate with drivers showing how much each value moves the prediction
Partial input: missing values filled from the 60 most similar patients, shown as a likely range
Model report with confusion matrix, ROC curve, model comparison and permutation importance
Hand-written SVG charts, dark mode and a mobile layout

images.caption: Partial input with an uncertainty range

projects.title: AutoEDA — Automated Data Analysis
projects.summary: Upload any dataset and get its exploratory analysis automatically: inferred column types, data-quality warnings, distributions, correlations and maps. Zomato's 9,551 restaurants are built in as a demo.
projects.description: What started as a Zomato EDA notebook became a tool that automates the analysis for any tabular file. It reads CSV, Excel, JSON (including nested API responses) and Parquet, detects encoding and delimiters, infers nine column types, and generates a full report with plain-language insights and a downloadable Markdown summary. The Zomato demo adds a guided analysis where every observation is computed from the data, and flags real errors in the source data.
features: Reads CSV/TSV, Excel, JSON, JSON Lines and Parquet; flattens nested JSON automatically
Infers numeric, categorical, boolean, datetime, multi-label, text, ID, constant and geo columns
Rule-based insights: missing data, zero-inflation, skew, outliers, dominant values and strong correlations
Correlation heatmaps, target-feature ranking (Spearman, η, Cramér's V), time series and maps
Found source errors in Zomato: wrong currency for the Philippines, 2,148 unrated rows, 497 rows at (0, 0)
Engine unit tests and headless UI tests across many kinds of dataset

images.caption: Automated report: overview and inferred types
